paper.abstract_en: We present an exact gravitational instanton solution on a five-dimensional, conformally invariant, Kerr-like warped Riemannian brane-world manifold. This geometry can be described as the Kähler manifold $\mathbb{C}^1\times\mathbb{C}^1\times \mathbb{R}$. By applying a double cover of $S^3$ through stereographic projection onto $\mathbb{C}P^1\times \mathbb{C}P^1$ of the effective four-dimensional manifold, together with the Klein surface construction, we exploit the underlying $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. The instanton is then obtained by fibering over the antipodal $S^2$. The metric is determined by a first-order differential equation containing an integer parameter, while the equation governing the angular momentum component decouples from the remaining field equations. We demonstrate that our solution can be transformed analytically into a locally conformally related Kähler manifold with a Kähler potential, thereby revealing the self-dual structure. Finally, we explore a potential connection with Penrose's model of gravity-induced collapse in entangled primordial spacetimes.
